items.summary: Kymera Therapeutics’ phase 2b eczema clinical trial has hit its primary endpoint and exceeded analyst expectations, teeing up further development of an oral drug candidate that could challenge Dupixent in a range of indications.

items.title: Arcus halts phase 3 pancreatic cancer study of CD73 inhibitor that looked destined to fail
items.summary: Arcus Biosciences has abandoned a phase 3 trial of quemliclustat after the small-molecule CD73 inhibitor looked unlikely to improve survival for pancreatic cancer.

items.title: Invivyd aims for Q1’27 submission after Pemgarda successor shows potential in phase 3
items.summary: Invivyd is planning to submit an approval application for its follow-up to the FDA-authorized monoclonal antibody Pemgarda in the first quarter of 2027 after hailing “high, durable antiviral activity” in a phase 3 trial.

items.title: Led by founders of J&J-acquired Intra-Cellular, Ritzey debuts with $112M for DYRK1A inhibitors
items.summary: The founder of Intra-Cellular Therapies, which was bought by Johnson & Johnson last year for $14.6 billion, is jumping back into the biotech fray with a new company similarly aimed at signaling pathways in the brain.

items.title: Lilly buys preclinical LoQus23 in $725M deal to zero in on Huntington’s target
items.summary: Eli Lilly has struck a deal to buy preclinical Huntington’s disease biotech LoQus23 Therapeutics for up to $725 million.

items.title: Capricor weathers second DMD cell therapy snub as FDA alleges 'serious' data integrity concerns
items.summary: Contrasting with the blunt release of the complete response letter that heralded the initial rejection of deramiocel last summer, the FDA appeared mindful of the optics Friday as it sought to explain why it turned down Capricor Therapeutics’ Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy for a second time.

items.title: Danaher teams up with Microsoft to boost ‘experimental execution’
items.summary: Danaher Corporation and Microsoft are teaming up for a strategic partnership to develop smart scientific instruments and an interoperable agentic ecosystem.

items.title: Merck’s TROP2 ADC extends survival in pivotal gastroesophageal cancer trial
items.summary: Merck & Co.’s sacituzumab tirumotecan has improved overall survival in a phase 3 cancer trial, delivering a second pivotal global victory for the TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate.

items.title: Researchers may have to ‘revise a lot’ of theories about dementia after uncovering plastics in brain
items.summary: The field of micro- and nanoplastics has drawn a lot of interest in recent years as concerns grow about the impact of contamination in the environment. These tiny plastic particles are created when plastic breaks down and are usually so small that they are invisible to the naked eye.

items.title: Bayer to pull kidney blockbuster Kerendia in Germany amid reimbursement dispute
items.summary: After a reimbursement dispute with German health regulators, Bayer is pulling its kidney disease and heart failure blockbuster Kerendia from the market there.

items.title: Bristol Myers' Sotyktu posts a hit and a miss in pair of ph. 3 lupus trials
items.summary: Results came across both good and less-so in topline readouts from two phase 3 Sotyktu trials in systemic lupus erythematosus Wednesday, with Bristol Myers Squibb offering a mixed outlook on its TYK2 inhibitor’s expansion prospects heading into the Thanksgiving holiday.

items.title: Cogent secures 2nd-line approval in rare GI cancer, the first in 20 years
items.summary: Cogent Biosciences’ kinase inhibitor secured FDA approval as a second-line treatment for patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors who have previously received imatinib. It’s the first new second-line treatment option in two decades.

items.title: GSK eyes approval filings after asthma med Exdensur scores in rare vascular disease
items.summary: Approaching one year since the medicine’s FDA approval, GSK is bolstering the case for its ultra-long-acting biologic Exdensur to help patients beyond its inaugural indication in severe asthma.

items.title: Orca deploys undisclosed number of layoffs amid focus on Tregzi launch
items.summary: Orca Bio is making cuts to its workforce just months after launching its first FDA-approved therapy, Tregzi.

items.title: CMS touts nearly $10B in savings potential as latest round of Medicare negotiated prices unveiled
items.summary: In its third round of negotiations, CMS achieved lower prices for 13 drugs under Medicare Part B and Part D. The price changes could have saved Medicare some $9.2 billion had they been in place in 2025, reflecting savings of 45%, the agency suggested.

items.title: TJC buys majority stake in healthcare events firm HMP to unleash M&A
items.summary: Private equity firm TJC is buying a majority interest in the healthcare events, education and engagement company HMP Global.

items.title: Rinvoq secures FDA nod in vitiligo, portending market showdown with Incyte
items.summary: AbbVie's immunology blockbuster Rinvoq secured an FDA nod in nonsegmental vitiligo, making it the first oral therapy approved for the condition and the first new targeted treatment to contend with Incyte's established therapy Opzelura.

items.title: Marksans Pharma flagged for 6 observations in wake of FDA inspection
items.summary: Indian drugmaker Marksans Pharma was cited over six observations in a Form 483 from the FDA.

items.title: Bristol Myers looks within for new CFO as David Elkins plots pivot to Coca-Cola
items.summary: Following some seven years as Bristol Myers Squibb’s chief financial officer, plus many more before that in the life sciences industry more broadly, David Elkins is trading the allure of Big Pharma for just about the biggest name there is in the world of refreshment.

items.title: BridgeBio breaks ground in inherited muscle disorder as first of 3 hoped-for FDA approvals arrives
items.summary: The first drug in BridgeBio’s hoped-for troika of new approvals has arrived, with the FDA on Monday giving the all-clear to ribitol, now christened Welgemda, as a targeted treatment for adults and kids with the rare genetic muscle disease limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9.

items.title: Novo nets NBA partnership, courting health education with the Philadelphia 76ers
items.summary: The multi-year partnership offers Novo digital, social and in-person opportunities to promote health education across the Philadelphia area, with fan activations and social media content already on the books.

items.title: Roche opens key early-stage breast cancer market for oral SERDs with Wilserdly FDA nod
items.summary: Roche’s Wilserdly has become the first oral SERD to be approved by the FDA in early-stage breast cancer, kicking off the drug class’s biggest commercial test yet in a post-surgery market that holds the bulk of its multibillion-dollar sales potential.

items.title: Breckenridge recalls US beta-blocker batch after suspected metal contamination
items.summary: Breckenridge Pharmaceutical is recalling one lot of 60-mg propranolol hydrochloride extended-release capsules, citing the potential for metal contamination.

items.title: Novartis girds $5B Leqvio sales forecast with early look at cardiovascular disease ph. 3 data
items.summary: After presenting a rosier sales forecast for its cholesterol medicine Leqvio last week, Novartis has offered an early taste of the PCSK9 blockbuster’s potential to reduce cardiovascular risk.

items.title: As FDA delay sent Savara stock tumbling, analysts point to potential agency 'bandwidth issues'
items.summary: On Friday, the FDA said it would miss a long-anticipated decision target for Savara's rare lung disease candidate. The delay came with little explanation, sending the biotech's shares tumbling ahead of the weekend, even as analysts estimated that the FDA's own capacity issues could be to blame.

items.title: Big pharmas ride GTA VI’s promotional coattails in tribute to global phenomenon
items.summary: What does the pharma industry have in common with gaming giant Rockstar Games and its promotional tour for its new major game, Grand Theft Auto VI?

items.title: Regulatory tracker: Novo's Sogroya wins 4th label expansion this year
items.summary: In this tracker, Fierce Pharma is recording the regulatory progress of in-market products, including expansions into key geographies and new indications. Some of these updates may not meet the bar for standalone stories, but we think they are still worth mentioning.

items.title: Merck scores US, German wins over Halozyme in Keytruda Qlex patent fight
items.summary: Merck & Co. has delivered a one-two legal punch against Halozyme Therapeutics, clearing major commercialization hurdles for subcutaneous Keytruda in the U.S. and Germany.

items.title: Mapping psychedelics’ commercial summit
items.summary: Several years after the FDA's high-profile rejection of Lykos Therapeutics’ MDMA candidate for post-traumatic stress disorder, a new wave of developers is nearing the regulatory finish line with experimental psychedelic treatments for mental health conditions. But regulatory approval is, in many ways, just the beginning of a complex journey to market for these companies, should their drugs pass mu…

items.title: The Oral GLP-1 Tracker: Foundayo holds steady as Wegovy pill takes a 5% dip
items.summary: Fierce Pharma is launching the weekly Oral GLP-1 Tracker, leveraging analysts’ notes and IQVIA data to monitor prescription trends and shifting market shares as Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill and Eli Lilly's Foundayo vie to become the go-to oral weight-loss solution for millions.

items.title: Another 215 layoffs linked to Novo's New Jersey HQ
items.summary: Novo will trim 215 jobs reporting to its New Jersey headquarters starting in February as part of a "redesign" of its U.S. sales organization.

items.title: FDA sets up new safety council to keep tabs on approved vaccines, cell and gene therapies
items.summary: The FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research is setting up a new governance body focused on safety oversight of products like cell and gene therapies and vaccines once they’ve hit the market.
